external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A person who writes changes, pushes branches, and can manually kick off a rebuild of main.
external_entities.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
external_entities.notes: The text does not state where developers are located or what authentication they use.

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
external_entities.notes: The text does not state the registry's authentication or encryption properties.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: Till software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container
processes.notes: The text does not state the technology, exposure, or interface presented by the till software.

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, pushes images, calls the deploy controller, and can be used to manually rebuild main.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: The runner uses a shared build token to call the deploy controller. The text does not state the runner's exposure or interface kind.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Records which image SHA the estate should be on and serves the current release to store servers.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.
processes.notes: The controller accepts calls from the build runner and requests from store servers. The text does not state its exposure or interface kind.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small server in the back office of each store that runs the till software as a container, polls the deploy controller, pulls images, and restarts the container when needed.
processes.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
processes.notes: The text does not state what a store server presents to the image registry or deploy controller.

data_stores.name: self-hosted git server
data_stores.description: Git server receiving developer branches and providing source for builds.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: Registry in the build environment that stores finished container images tagged with commit SHAs and serves them to store servers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores. The text does not state what a store server presents to the registry when pulling.

data_stores.name: release record
data_stores.description: The record identifying which image SHA the estate should be on.
data_stores.source_excerpt: holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on
data_stores.notes: The text says the deploy controller holds this record but does not separately place the record in a zone.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: Developer pushes a branch to the self-hosted git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: start build
data_flows.description: A merge to main starts a build picked up by the build runner.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A merge to `main` is what starts a build.
data_flows.notes: The text does not describe the mechanism by which the merge starts the build.

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source from the self-hosted git server.

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches out to the public package registry while resolving dependencies.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.data_description: container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: make release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.

data_flows.name: ask release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller for the current release once a minute.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: The text does not state what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current image from the image registry when its running image differs from the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it pulls that image from the registry and restarts the container
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull, but the text does not state what a store server presents to it.

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually kicks off a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed. The text does not state the login authentication mechanism.
